seoTitle: Staying After Graduation: Residence Pathways in Four Countries
title: Staying After Graduation: Residence Pathways in Four Countries
content:
Graduating does not automatically give you permanent residence. Plan around the current route from student status to employment or another eligible status, then check the conditions for longer-term residence.

A degree is not a residence guarantee

Separate three decisions: where you want to study, what permission you may have after graduation and how you might qualify for longer-term residence. A university admission offer answers only the first of those questions. The immigration route depends on the rules and your circumstances when you apply.

Canada

Check whether your programme and institution meet the current post-graduation work permit requirements. Later permanent-residence routes have their own conditions and selection processes. A Canadian qualification or work permit does not by itself guarantee selection through an economic immigration programme.

Australia

A Temporary Graduate visa and a skilled migration route are different permissions. Eligibility can depend on qualifications, personal circumstances and other conditions. If a later route involves an occupation assessment, nomination or invitation, investigate those requirements separately rather than assuming the degree completes them.

Germany

Check the available route after your studies and the conditions for moving into qualifying work. Longer-term residence depends on the relevant permit and requirements, which can include employment and other evidence. Use the official Make it in Germany guidance and the responsible authority's instructions for your situation.

United Kingdom

The Graduate route provides temporary permission where eligibility conditions are met. It is not itself a guarantee of settlement or future sponsorship. A later work route has separate requirements. Also read any scholarship conditions that require you to leave the UK after the award.

Build a plan you can update

  • Find the official student and post-study route pages for your circumstances.
  • Check the work conditions and the timing for each application.
  • Research realistic jobs for your field, including employer sponsorship where relevant.
  • Record the requirements of the longer-term route separately.
  • Revisit the plan before graduation and before changing immigration status.

Choose a course you can afford and that makes academic and professional sense even if a particular residence route changes. For an individual immigration decision, obtain advice from the relevant authority or an appropriately qualified adviser. A broad comparison cannot determine a person's eligibility.

Official information

  • Canada: immigration and citizenship
  • Australia: official visa information
  • Germany: settlement guidance
  • UK: Graduate visa

Ask what the next status would require

A useful residence plan starts with the next eligible status, not a promise of permanent residence. If employment is part of the route, check the job, salary or qualification conditions relevant to that permission. Also check how student time is treated and whether other requirements apply. Record uncertain points as questions for official guidance or a qualified adviser. Rules can change during a multi-year degree, so review the plan at important stages rather than treating today’s requirements as a guarantee of your position at graduation.

Relevant listings and guides on NextApply

To see how these questions apply to a real listing, review NDA PhD Studentship: Guardrails for AI in the Nuclear Sector at Lancaster University. Compare its stated requirements with your own preparation and check the official source before applying.

You can also browse Lancaster University on NextApply and the PhD positions category. Listings and recruitment windows can change.
